basis: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells defines this diabetes subtype; diabetic end-organ complications are separate diseases.
Immune-mediated epidermal injury with defining mucositis; damaging oral erosions occur in most patients. Ocular damage is less common.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across clinically affected Xp duplication syndromes; other organ malformations vary by duplicated segment.
Developmental delay in 5/5 and intellectual disability in 4/4 define the syndrome. Ocular lesions and lymphopenia have single-patient assessments; common involvement is uncertain.
Neoplasm originates in the nasopharynx, part of the upper respiratory airway.
Benign epithelial tumour arising in cutaneous sweat glands.
Defined by multiple central nervous system phenotypes, including intellectual disability, autism and seizures; other malformations are unspecified.
TTN-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; skeletal muscle disease is not established for this cardiac subtype.
Neurodevelopmental delay, intellectual disability, microcephaly and structural brain abnormalities define the disorder.
Neurological mislocalization of sensory stimuli; no intrinsic damage to the stimulated organ is implied.
Dysplastic adenomatous neoplasm arising in colonic epithelium.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across symptomatic 10q deletion syndromes; other organ defects depend on deletion location and extent.
Central and peripheral neurological degeneration defines the disease. Weakness and distal amyotrophy accompany neuropathy; independent common muscle or eye damage is unproven.
Progressive language dysfunction from frontotemporal neurodegeneration; the reported skin fold is not damaging skin disease.
Congenital structural anomaly of the atrial appendages.
Infection directly affects the nail.
Localized cutaneous lymphatic lesion; no separate blood-vessel or systemic organ involvement is established.
Sodium-losing enteropathy causes defining electrolyte and acid-base disturbances; choanal atresia and recurrent corneal erosions are common syndromic features, each reported in >30%.
Defining lacrimal drainage stenosis with dacryocystitis and osteopoikilotic bone lesions.
Congenital absence of the uterine cervix is confined to reproductive anatomy outside the axes.
Chronic follicular inflammation causes fibrotic papules, keloidal scarring and local hair loss; infection is not intrinsic to the diagnosis.
Defining digital skeletal malformations and congenital nail dysplasia; breast hypertrophy lies outside the axes.
The described syndrome combines absent hair and abnormal nails, preaxial polydactyly and thin dental enamel; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital aortic valve dysfunction with incomplete closure and regurgitation.
Central ocular motor disorder with ataxia and developmental impairment. Eye movement abnormalities do not establish intrinsic eye damage; amblyopia occurs in 1/9.
